sections.label: Cess Act amended 2008
sections.summary: The Cess Act was amended in 2008 to link cess to specific tourism events, so cess is imposed only on tourist hotels during the Formula One Singapore Grand Prix.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Cess Act was amended in 2008 to make cess more targeted by linking it to specific tourism events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Since then, cess has only been imposed on tourist hotels during the period of the Formula One Singapore Grand Prix.

sections.label: Flexibility for future business models
sections.summary: The changes provide flexibility for future business models and industry trends, with no current plans for new tourism events or establishment categories.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We are making these changes to the Act to provide flexibility to deal with future changes in business models and industry trends.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: There are no current plans to include new tourism events or to impose cess on new categories of tourism event establishments, beyond the Singapore Grand Prix or hotels respectively.

sections.label: Records retention period increased
sections.summary: Under clause 6, the records retention period increases from two to five years, aligned with the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Under clause 6, the records retention period will be increased from two to five years, which is aligned to the requirements under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act.

sections.label: Act last amended August 2008
sections.summary: The Act was last amended in August 2008 before the inaugural F1 race, changed from a consumption tax to a business tax for strategic tourist events.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Act was last amended in August 2008, just months before the inaugural F1 race.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was changed from a consumption tax to a business tax to be used in a targeted manner to fund strategic tourist events.

sections.label: Cess collected versus F1 co-funding
sections.summary: The passage asks how much cess was collected in the last 10 years compared to expenditure of co-funding the F1.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How much cess was collected in the last 10 years compared to the expenditure of co-funding the F1?

sections.label: Cess into Tourism Development Fund
sections.summary: The speaker says having cess go directly into the Tourism Development Fund may be symbolic, since Government funding likely exceeded proceeds, but it signals the public.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Having the collected cess go directly into the Tourism Development Fund may be just symbolic in the end, since I suspect Government funding of the event exceeded the proceeds, but it sends an important signal to the public.

sections.label: Formula One Singapore Grand Prix renewal
sections.summary: The Formula One Singapore Grand Prix was renewed for four years from 2018 to 2021, with a direct organising cost of about $135 million yearly and a 60% Government share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Last September, we renewed the Formula One Singapore Grand Prix for another four years from 2018 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The direct cost of organising the race is around $135 million per year, with the Government’s share at 60%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years of hosting the race, we have attracted more than 450,000 international visitors, contributing about $1.4 billion in incremental tourism receipts.
